title: Knowledge Check 4 - Lessons 16-20
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 16-20 - Prompt Engineering | Data 360 Fundamentals. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: In what order does Agentforce determine which model a subagent uses?
options: The org default, then the agent, then the subagent
The subagent, then the agent, then the model selected in Setup
The prompt template, then the subagent, then the org default
Always the org default only
questions.explanation: Agentforce checks the subagent model first, then the agent model, then the model selected in Setup, so a subagent override beats an agent override, which beats the org default.

questions.question: An author opens a prompt template that points at a model the admin just hid. What do they see and can the template still run?
options: The template is blocked until the model is shown again
The template is deleted automatically
The model runs but silently switches to the org default
The model is shown as hidden and the template runs the same as before
questions.explanation: A hidden model does not stop a template that already uses it; those templates run as before, and the author sees the model marked hidden and non-selectable rather than an error.

questions.question: A subagent uses a model override, and an action in that agent runs a prompt template. Which model does the prompt template use?
options: The model configured on the prompt template itself, which model override does not change
The subagent's override model
The agent-level override model
Always the org default, ignoring the template
questions.explanation: Model override does not affect the model that prompt templates in actions use, so the template runs on its own configured model regardless of the subagent or agent override.

questions.question: What separates an Agentforce Data Library from a Salesforce Knowledge base?
options: A data library only indexes published Knowledge articles.
A data library wraps sources such as Knowledge articles, uploaded files and custom retrievers into searchable chunks.
A data library replaces Data 360 and needs no indexing.
A data library stores documents inside the agent's prompt template.
questions.explanation: A library is a broader retrieval layer that can index content beyond Knowledge articles, while the other options misdescribe either its sources or its dependency on Data 360.

questions.question: Before you can create an Agentforce Data Library in an org, what must be true?
options: Knowledge must be enabled and no other product is needed.
Prompt Builder must be licensed and Data 360 is optional.
A vector database must be provisioned by the customer outside Data 360.
Data 360 must be set up and activated, because every library builds objects inside it.
questions.explanation: Every library provisions a data stream, search index and retriever inside Data 360, and libraries consume Data 360 credits, so Data 360 is a prerequisite.

questions.question: An agent must answer from a specific retriever you configured in Data 360 rather than the auto-built one. What do you use?
options: A custom retriever referenced by your own prompt template.
The Answer Questions with Knowledge action with no retriever input.
A web search data library, which is read-only.
A Knowledge data category on the source article.
questions.explanation: A custom retriever wired into your own prompt template gives control over which datasets are reached, whereas the packaged action uses the retriever Salesforce builds for the library.

questions.question: Which object references your unstructured files without copying them into Salesforce?
options: Unstructured data lake object (UDLO).
Data model object (DMO).
Data stream.
Search index.
questions.explanation: A UDLO references unstructured data in an external blob store and holds its metadata, while the DMO is the modeled shape and the data stream is the connection that ingests structured data.

questions.question: Chunking for a new Knowledge based library is taking much longer than expected. Which factor most directly explains the duration?
options: The number of data spaces in the org.
The number of permission sets assigned to agents.
The number, size and complexity of articles or files and the number of knowledge fields selected for chunking.
The version of the large language model behind the agent.
questions.explanation: Chunking time scales with the volume and complexity of the content and the number of knowledge fields you selected, not with org licensing or model version.

questions.question: Which data library source creates a retriever but no search index?
options: Uploaded PDF files.
Knowledge articles.
A custom retriever source.
Web search.
questions.explanation: A web search library is read-only and fetches content live, so it creates only a retriever and skips the chunk-and-index chain.

questions.question: At runtime, what happens first when a user asks an agent a question tied to a data library?
options: The content is rechunked and reindexed.
The user's query is added to the prompt template, which references the retriever.
A new data stream is created for the question.
The large language model answers directly with no retrieval.
questions.explanation: The query is folded into the prompt template that references the retriever, which then searches the index and adds the relevant chunks.

questions.question: Which statement about retrievers and search indexes is correct?
options: A search index can be shared only if the libraries first share a retriever.
A retriever stores the embeddings and the index points to it.
Web search libraries create a search index and a retriever.
Each data library has its own retriever, and retrievers can point to the same search index while each pointer stays unique.
questions.explanation: Each library gets its own retriever, and multiple retrievers may point at one search index, so sharing an index is fine while sharing a retriever is not.

questions.question: For a file or knowledge based library, when is the retriever created?
options: After chunking completes and the search index is ready.
Before the data stream is created.
When the first user asks a question.
As soon as the library is named and saved.
questions.explanation: The retriever is created only after chunking finishes and the search index is ready, so a stalled index means no retriever exists yet.

questions.question: Reps can open the agent but get no answers grounded in the library, which is otherwise healthy. Which grant is most likely missing?
options: The Data Cloud User permission with the default data space added.
The Manage Bots permission.
The Manage Data Libraries permission.
A Knowledge data category on the source article.
questions.explanation: The running user needs Data Cloud User with the default data space to reach the retriever, while Manage Data Libraries is a setup permission that does not grant retrieval.

questions.question: A Knowledge based library answers most questions but never returns content from one indexed field. What should you check first?
options: The length of the library name.
Whether the agent uses the Service Planner.
Field level security on that indexed field for the running user.
The number of data spaces in the org.
questions.explanation: Retrieval respects field permissions, so a field the running user cannot read is dropped from the index results even though the article contains it.

questions.question: External Community users cannot retrieve from a library that works for internal users. What is the fix?
options: Add the external users to the Manage Data Libraries permission.
Recreate the search index.
Grant Allow View Knowledge to the external users.
Tag the library's data model objects ExternalData.Visibility.Portal or ExternalData.Visibility.Public.
questions.explanation: Internal users are covered by the All Data Access ruleset policy, but external users need the library's data model objects tagged for external visibility.
